newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa sees 1996 profits down 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees 1996 profits down 10 pct.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa is likely to report a profit for 1996 which will be at least 10 percent below last year's level, Klaus Schlede, the company's chief financial officer said on Thursday.
Schlede told a news conference, "We expect in the best case that profits for this year will be 10 percent below those last year."
He added however that if the airline managed to reduce its costs as planned, it expected that 1997 would bring "a significant improvement in its profits".
Schlede said that Lufthansa's freight business which turned to loss in the first nine months of the year would continue to be loss-making in 1997 but was expected to make a profit in 1998.
"We will be back in the black in 1998," Schlede said.

Earlier, Lufthansa said group pre-tax profit fell to 434 million marks in the first nine months of 1996 compared with 506 million for the same 1995 period. Group operating profit fell to 408 million marks from 523 million marks.
